title: Named Driver Exclusion Endorsement — Owner Auto Policy Conditions
content:
**Who signs.** The Named Driver Exclusion form for an Owner Auto Policy is signed only by the named insured personally. That the named insured is the one signing rests on the caller's own statement.

**What the endorsement rests on.** A named driver exclusion is endorsed only on a Named Driver Exclusion form signed by the named insured that names the driver exactly as the driver is to be excluded. The signed form is identified in the company's records and is the one the endorsement references.

**Who cannot be excluded.**
- The named insured cannot be excluded.
- A driver for whom an SR-22 or FR-44 certificate backed by this term is filed cannot be excluded. This is read from the company's filing records for the term.

**Excluded-driver cap.** The number of currently excluded drivers on the term must be below the package's maximum before another exclusion is endorsed. Currently excluded drivers are counted as the distinct drivers whose most recent change on the term, effective on or before today, is an exclusion. The maximum for each package is in the policy structure limits.

**Effective date.**
- The clause "The exclusion takes effect on the later of the date the form was signed and the requested effective date on the form, never earlier than the signing date" is no longer in force as a rule for every exclusion.
- For the exclusion of the resident named on the term's latest Named Driver Exclusion form by signing date, the exclusion takes effect on the date the company sets for that endorsement, never earlier than the signing date. This applies when that resident is reported operating a scheduled vehicle on a claim of the term while unlisted and carries no driver-added entry on the term.
- The exclusion of any other driver still takes effect on the later of the date the form was signed and the requested effective date on the form, never earlier than the signing date.
- An exclusion stays in force on the term, and on every renewal, until the driver is added back as a rated driver.

**Premium.**
- The clause "When the driver was rated immediately before the exclusion, premium is returned as a return premium entry; when the driver was unlisted, there is no premium change" is no longer in force as a rule for every exclusion.
- The reported resident described above is first listed as a rated driver and then excluded, in one endorsement, and is charged a listing premium for the days between.
- For any other driver, including a resident once rated on the term by a driver-added entry:
  - when the driver was rated immediately before the exclusion, premium is returned as a return premium entry;
  - when the driver was unlisted, there is no premium change;
  - no listing premium is charged.

**Effect on coverage.** While an excluded driver operates any vehicle, the policy provides no coverage of any kind for that use, and claims are decided accordingly.

**Household members not listed.** A household member who must be listed and is neither rated nor excluded must be added as a rated driver, subject to package acceptability.
